what_it_does: Zero-knowledge proofs (ZKPs) are a cryptographic technique that lets one party convince another that a computation was done correctly — without revealing any of the underlying private data. They underpin privacy features in blockchains and can make AI inference verifiable. Generating a single ZKP is very computationally expensive (involving operations like multi-scalar multiplication and number-theoretic transforms — complex arithmetic on very large integers), and while GPUs have been used to speed up single proof generation, no existing system was designed to churn out many proofs simultaneously at high throughput. BatchZK builds a fully pipelined GPU execution engine: proof generation is broken into multiple sequential stages, and the GPU processes many different proofs at the same time by keeping each stage busy with a different proof — like an assembly line where every station is always working on something. GPU 'streams' (independent execution queues) and careful memory management keep the GPU's compute units continuously occupied, amortizing the fixed overhead of launching operations across the whole batch. The result is much higher proofs-per-second throughput without sacrificing individual proof correctness.
